claims.text: The charge stands or falls on POL-NS-01(c): the driver must have held position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous dwell of at least 300 seconds for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. On the platform's own derived figures the longest continuous qualifying run is 170 seconds — the first interval in the bay runs 19:00:00 to 19:02:50 and the second 19:03:50 to 19:06:30. Neither interval, taken on its own, comes close to the 300-second minimum, so limb (c) is not satisfied by the driver's actual, continuous conduct.

The two intervals are genuinely separate because the driver left the bay between them: the trace records a 60-second excursion from 19:02:50 to 19:03:50 in which the driver reached 179.8 m from the pickup pin and was recorded at 24 km/h — travelling during the waiting period, not holding position. A wait broken by a 60-second, roughly 180-metre departure is not the unbroken hold that POL-NS-01(c) requires.

On the rider's case the effective in-geofence dwell is the 170-second continuous run — 130 seconds short of the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum — and POL-NS-06 then provides that the cancellation fee is 'not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The rider's own device sitting 519 m from the pin, and the absence of any rider message in the chat log, are therefore immaterial to this clause and cannot be used to prop up the charge.

The only figure that reaches 300 seconds is the accumulated 330 seconds, and that figure exists solely because POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed where a qualifying traffic advisory made holding position unlawful. That provision is a computation rule for the shortfall test in POL-NS-06; it does not enact a continuous dwell, and the continuous-dwell condition in POL-NS-01(c) remains a separate condition of chargeability. The advisory in force — a MODERATE kerb closure whose own description tells vehicles to 'circulate before returning to the marked bay' — explains why the driver left, but it does not convert two short waits into a single 300-second hold.

The driver's own account corroborates a broken wait rather than a continuous hold: he messaged at 19:02:30 that the kerb was temporarily closed and that he 'must circulate and will return to the same bay', and again at 19:04:05 that he was 'back at the marked bay now'. That is the same 60-second departure the trace shows, and it is inconsistent with an unbroken 300-second hold in the bay.

Compensation to the driver can only follow a POL-NS-01 that is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-07 says so expressly. Where the effective dwell falls short, POL-NS-06 provides that the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable. The rider therefore asks that the SGD 4.00 charged be returned and that nothing be paid to the driver out of it, the fare record confirming the fee was charged and not reversed.

The driver's own trace satisfies the POL-NS-02 arrival test many times over: 35 of his 40 fixes are qualifying in-radius fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, against a requirement of only three consecutive in-radius fixes at 25 m accuracy or better. The 'arrived' event at 19:00:20 is corroborated by the trace, not contradicted by it.

The rider's entire case is that the two waits may not be added together. POL-NS-06(i) says they may be: the driver's two in-geofence intervals of 170 s (19:00:00 to 19:02:50) and 160 s (19:03:50 to 19:06:30) accumulate to 330 s, 30 s past the 300 s LARGE_VENUE minimum, so there is no shortfall and the fee is not displaced.

Aggregation is available because the qualifying advisory is actually present and populated, not asserted against a missing artifact: EV-ADVIS-09107-01 carries type CLOSURE, one of the four admissible types, its geometry covers the pickup road and its active window of 18:50 to 19:30 covers the whole waiting period from 19:00 to 19:06:30.

The circulation never amounted to abandoning the pickup attempt. The driver's furthest point between the two intervals was 179.8 m from the pin, well inside the 300 m leash POL-NS-06(i) sets, so the separate intervals are properly summed rather than treated as two failed waits.

The chat log confirms the circulation was a kerbside manoeuvre, not a departure from the job: the driver wrote at 19:02:30 that the kerb was temporarily closed and that he must circulate and would return to the same bay, and at 19:04:05 that he was back at the marked bay. That is a party statement in the chat log and it corroborates the sequence the trace shows.

No rider-side exoneration under POL-NS-04 is available. Limb (a) requires a rider locating or coordinating message during the waiting window, and the chat log holds none from the rider at all, only the system 'driver has arrived' alert and the driver's two messages.

POL-NS-04(c) is not merely undecidable, it is affirmatively failed: 0 of the rider's 19 fixes were qualifying against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, and the rider's device sits roughly 519 m from the pin throughout the waiting window. The rider was not waiting at the pickup point.

The termination limb is met: the trip record shows cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, cancelled by the driver at 19:06:30, after the 300 s dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event recorded anywhere in the trip record.

There is no false-arrival marker to correct. The 'arrived' event is 20 seconds after the first qualifying in-geofence fix, the driver was stationary in the bay at that moment and nowhere near the 300 m trigger, so POL-NS-05 does not recompute the waiting clock and the dwell stands as computed.

The fee charged is exactly the fee schedule figure and survives POL-NS-08(d): the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee is 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is 4.00, the greater of the two is 4.00, and the fare breakdown's cancellation_fee line is 4.00 with no refund issued.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is owed 80 percent of the 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 120 completed_trips_30d is 0.0083, below 0.08. Compensation is therefore paid and the charge stands.

No escalation trigger is engaged. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and the riders' and driver's disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, the anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip, and every artifact in the bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so none of POL-NS-09(a) to (e) applies and the dispute can be decided on the money.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show fee charged for trip TRP-09107 on 7 Sep 2026 stands, and the driver is paid SGD 3.20 of it.

Chargeability. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 19:00:20 and shows the trip terminated by the driver at 19:06:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event (POL-NS-01(a) and (d)). The GPS trace places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from 19:00:00 — 20 seconds before the marker — with 35 of his 40 fixes qualifying at the 25 m accuracy filter, far more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires (POL-NS-01(b)). The arrival marker is not false: at 19:00:20 the driver was stationary in the bay, not 300 m from the pin and not travelling at 15 km/h, so POL-NS-05 does not recompute the waiting clock.

The rider's case, answered. The rider argues that the driver left the bay from 19:02:50 to 19:03:50 — a 60-second circulation reaching 179.8 m and 24 km/h — that the longest continuous run is only 170 seconds, that the two waits cannot be added, and that limb (c)'s 300-second minimum is therefore missed; the rider adds that the kerb-closure advisory explains the break but does not convert two short waits into one 300-second hold. That reading is rejected. POL-NS-06(i) expressly permits dwell to be accumulated across separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt where (1) the driver never travels more than 300 m from the pin and (2) a qualifying traffic advisory whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the waiting period is present with an admissible type. Both conditions hold on this record: the furthest point of the circulation was 179.8 m, inside the 300 m leash, and EV-ADVIS-09107-01 is present and populated with type CLOSURE — one of the four admissible types — its geometry covering the pickup road and its 18:50–19:30 window covering the whole wait. The intervals therefore sum to 330 seconds (170 + 160), 30 seconds past the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, and the shortfall that alone would trigger a refund under POL-NS-06 does not arise. The driver's own chat messages ('kerb is temporarily closed; I must circulate and will return to the same bay' at 19:02:30 and 'Back at the marked bay now' at 19:04:05) corroborate the sequence the trace shows but do not change the computation the clause prescribes. POL-NS-04 gives the rider no independent relief: the chat log holds no rider message at all, so limb (a) fails, and the rider device's 519 m distance from the pin is immaterial to this clause in any event.

Compensation. With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 applies: 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee itemised in the fare breakdown is SGD 3.20. The anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 120 completed_trips_30d is 0.0083, below 0.08 — so compensation is paid. The emitted ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.20 as driver_compensation_sgd; the rider's charge itself stands. The rider's request for the SGD 4.00 back with nothing paid to the driver is not supported.

Escalation and integrity. No escalation trigger is engaged: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, the same-pair dispute counts are 0, the anti-farming check is clear and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08 — the arrival marker is not clock-skewed against the trace (same 19:00:20), there are 40 fixes with no gap, the chat log's three messages match chat_message_count and its msg_id sequence is unbroken, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule (the greater of the SGD 4.00 LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the SGD 4.00 RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee). Every artifact in the bundle carries weight 1.0, so nothing is discounted. No clause produces a referral.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' accounts and the platform telemetry agree on the sequence at the Orchard Central marked ride-hail bay. The driver arrived about 19:00, the platform logged 'arrived' at 19:00:20, a kerb closure (EV-ADVIS-09107-01, type CLOSURE, active 18:50-19:30, geometry covering the pickup road and window covering the wait) forced one short circulation from 19:02:50 to 19:03:50 - peaking 179.8 m from the pin - and he returned to the same bay at 19:04:05, remaining until he cancelled at 19:06:30 with RIDER_NO_SHOW.

The rider is right on the raw facts: the two in-bay stretches (170 s from 19:00:00 to 19:02:50, and 160 s from 19:03:50 to 19:06:30) are each far short of the 300 s LARGE_VENUE minimum, and POL-NS-01(c) speaks of a continuous dwell. But POL-NS-06(i) is the provision that governs how dwell is counted where a qualifying traffic advisory made holding position unlawful: it expressly permits separate in-geofence intervals within a single pickup attempt to be summed, provided the driver never travelled more than 300 m from the pin. Both conditions are met - the advisory is present and populated with an admissible type (CLOSURE) and covers the pickup road and the waiting period, and the driver's furthest point was 179.8 m, inside the 300 m leash. The intervals therefore accumulate to 330 s, 30 s above the 300 s minimum, and there is no shortfall for POL-NS-06 to refund. The rider's central argument - that POL-NS-06(i) is merely a computation rule for the shortfall test and cannot satisfy POL-NS-01(c) - is rejected: it is precisely the rule that makes the summed time count towards the POL-NS-01 minimum, and reading it the other way would leave the fee neither chargeable under POL-NS-01 nor refundable under POL-NS-06. The rider's related points (the 60-second, 179.8 m, 24 km/h excursion and the driver's own chat messages at 19:02:30 and 19:04:05 describing the circulation) are accepted as facts but do not defeat aggregation.

The remaining conditions of chargeability hold. Thirty-five qualifying fixes at 25 m accuracy or better place the driver inside the 120 m arrival radius before the arrived event, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied and the dispute turns on dwell. There is no false-arrival marker: the arrived event is 20 s after the first qualifying in-geofence fix and nothing is near the 300 m or 15 km/h triggers (POL-NS-05). The termination limb is met: no boarding event and a driver cancellation coded RIDER_NO_SHOW at 19:06:30, after the minimum elapsed (POL-NS-01(d)). The fee reconciles with the schedule - the greater of the LARGE_VENUE 4.00 and RYDE_X 4.00 is 4.00, matching the fare line - so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. No POL-NS-04 exoneration applies: the rider sent no locating or coordinating message, and her device sat about 519 m from the pin throughout the wait, outside the 150 m rider-presence radius. POL-NS-03 does not apply either, because the driver did hold position inside the arrival radius, and with registered_pickup_points at 1 the pin-ambiguity goodwill of POL-NS-03(ii) is not available.

The SGD 4.00 fee therefore stands and the rider's claim is not supported. Because the charge stands, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee: SGD 3.20. ledger.claim: The charge stands or falls on POL-NS-01(c): the driver must have held position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous dwell of at least 300 seconds for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. On the platform's own derived figures the longest continuous qualifying run is 170 seconds — the first interval in the bay runs 19:00:00 to 19:02:50 and the second 19:03:50 to 19:06:30. Neither interval, taken on its own, comes close to the 300-second minimum, so limb (c) is not satisfied by the driver's actual, continuous conduct.

The two intervals are genuinely separate because the driver left the bay between them: the trace records a 60-second excursion from 19:02:50 to 19:03:50 in which the driver reached 179.8 m from the pickup pin and was recorded at 24 km/h — travelling during the waiting period, not holding position. A wait broken by a 60-second, roughly 180-metre departure is not the unbroken hold that POL-NS-01(c) requires.

On the rider's case the effective in-geofence dwell is the 170-second continuous run — 130 seconds short of the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum — and POL-NS-06 then provides that the cancellation fee is 'not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The rider's own device sitting 519 m from the pin, and the absence of any rider message in the chat log, are therefore immaterial to this clause and cannot be used to prop up the charge.

The only figure that reaches 300 seconds is the accumulated 330 seconds, and that figure exists solely because POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed where a qualifying traffic advisory made holding position unlawful. That provision is a computation rule for the shortfall test in POL-NS-06; it does not enact a continuous dwell, and the continuous-dwell condition in POL-NS-01(c) remains a separate condition of chargeability. The advisory in force — a MODERATE kerb closure whose own description tells vehicles to 'circulate before returning to the marked bay' — explains why the driver left, but it does not convert two short waits into a single 300-second hold.

The driver's own account corroborates a broken wait rather than a continuous hold: he messaged at 19:02:30 that the kerb was temporarily closed and that he 'must circulate and will return to the same bay', and again at 19:04:05 that he was 'back at the marked bay now'. That is the same 60-second departure the trace shows, and it is inconsistent with an unbroken 300-second hold in the bay.

Compensation to the driver can only follow a POL-NS-01 that is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-07 says so expressly. Where the effective dwell falls short, POL-NS-06 provides that the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable. The rider therefore asks that the SGD 4.00 charged be returned and that nothing be paid to the driver out of it, the fare record confirming the fee was charged and not reversed.

The driver's own trace satisfies the POL-NS-02 arrival test many times over: 35 of his 40 fixes are qualifying in-radius fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, against a requirement of only three consecutive in-radius fixes at 25 m accuracy or better. The 'arrived' event at 19:00:20 is corroborated by the trace, not contradicted by it.

The rider's entire case is that the two waits may not be added together. POL-NS-06(i) says they may be: the driver's two in-geofence intervals of 170 s (19:00:00 to 19:02:50) and 160 s (19:03:50 to 19:06:30) accumulate to 330 s, 30 s past the 300 s LARGE_VENUE minimum, so there is no shortfall and the fee is not displaced.

Aggregation is available because the qualifying advisory is actually present and populated, not asserted against a missing artifact: EV-ADVIS-09107-01 carries type CLOSURE, one of the four admissible types, its geometry covers the pickup road and its active window of 18:50 to 19:30 covers the whole waiting period from 19:00 to 19:06:30.

The circulation never amounted to abandoning the pickup attempt. The driver's furthest point between the two intervals was 179.8 m from the pin, well inside the 300 m leash POL-NS-06(i) sets, so the separate intervals are properly summed rather than treated as two failed waits.

The chat log confirms the circulation was a kerbside manoeuvre, not a departure from the job: the driver wrote at 19:02:30 that the kerb was temporarily closed and that he must circulate and would return to the same bay, and at 19:04:05 that he was back at the marked bay. That is a party statement in the chat log and it corroborates the sequence the trace shows.

No rider-side exoneration under POL-NS-04 is available. Limb (a) requires a rider locating or coordinating message during the waiting window, and the chat log holds none from the rider at all, only the system 'driver has arrived' alert and the driver's two messages.

POL-NS-04(c) is not merely undecidable, it is affirmatively failed: 0 of the rider's 19 fixes were qualifying against the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, and the rider's device sits roughly 519 m from the pin throughout the waiting window. The rider was not waiting at the pickup point.

The termination limb is met: the trip record shows cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, cancelled by the driver at 19:06:30, after the 300 s dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event recorded anywhere in the trip record.

There is no false-arrival marker to correct. The 'arrived' event is 20 seconds after the first qualifying in-geofence fix, the driver was stationary in the bay at that moment and nowhere near the 300 m trigger, so POL-NS-05 does not recompute the waiting clock and the dwell stands as computed.

The fee charged is exactly the fee schedule figure and survives POL-NS-08(d): the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee is 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is 4.00, the greater of the two is 4.00, and the fare breakdown's cancellation_fee line is 4.00 with no refund issued.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is owed 80 percent of the 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 120 completed_trips_30d is 0.0083, below 0.08. Compensation is therefore paid and the charge stands.
